item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15

12 leaders of APEC economies to attend APEC CEO Summit 2026 (Xinhua) 13:40, November 15, 2026 SHENZHEN, Nov. 15 (Xinhua) -- Twelve leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies will attend the APEC CEO Summit 2026, which is scheduled to be held from Nov. 17 to 18 in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) said Sunday. Chinese President Xi Jinping, along with leaders from APEC economies Australia, Canada, Chile, China's Hong Kong, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam, will attend the summit and deliver speeches or remarks, or participate in panel discussions, said Li Qingshuang, vice chairperson of the CCPIT, at a press conference. Representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies to attend APEC CEO Summit 2026 (Xinhua) 13:40, November 15, 2026 SHENZHEN, Nov. 15 (Xinhua) -- Representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies will attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) said Sunday. U.S. companies make up the largest group among participating companies from economies other than China, accounting for nearly 20 percent of the total, said Li Qingshuang, vice chairperson of the CCPIT, at a press conference. Heads of several international organizations, as well as leaders of business associations from the United States, Russia, Japan and other economies, will also attend the summit, Li said. item.title: How Chinese innovation drives shared growth from Shenzhen to Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
How Chinese innovation drives shared growth from Shenzhen to Asia-Pacific * Shenzhen offers a snapshot of this vibrant high-tech trade story. Total R&D spending in the city grew at an average annual rate of 12.9 percent from 2020 to 2024, and R&D intensity reached 6.67 percent, the highest among Chinese cities. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster has also topped the Global Innovation Index rankings. * Cooperation between Shenzhen and its Asia-Pacific partners advances along a well-defined track, featuring manufacturing, research and talent development, and the practical application of technology, said Chen Jiaxi, vice president of the Shenzhen Reform and Opening Up Executive Leadership Academy. * "The Shenzhen meeting will send a clear signal: China's commitment to high-standard opening up, to sharing opportunities with the Asia-Pacific, and to multilateralism remains firm," said Chen, who is also a professor at Shenzhen University. SHENZHEN, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- From a battery anode materials plant built from scratch in Indonesia to a surgical robot in a Kuala Lumpur operating room and solar panels atop a century-old Thai university, companies from China's southern tech hub of Shenzhen have established a presence across the Asia-Pacific region. Next week, as Shenzhen in Guangdong Province hosts the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the innovative, collaborative approach that Shenzhen embodies will take center stage. The numbers are significant. China's goods trade with other APEC members reached 26.29 trillion yuan (about 3.9 trillion U.S. dollars) in 2025, or nearly 60 percent of its total foreign trade, according to the General Administration of Customs. High-tech goods are an increasingly strong link: China's exports of such products to other APEC members rose 8.1 percent to 4.63 trillion yuan in 2025. Shenzhen offers a snapshot of this vibrant high-tech trade story. Total R&D spending in the city grew at an average annual rate of 12.9 percent from 2020 to 2024, and R&D intensity reached 6.67 percent, the highest among Chinese cities. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster has also topped the Global Innovation Index rankings. Cooperation between Shenzhen and its Asia-Pacific partners advances along a well-defined track, featuring manufacturing, research and talent development, and the practical application of technology, said Chen Jiaxi, vice president of the Shenzhen Reform and Opening Up Executive Leadership Academy. "The Shenzhen meeting will send a clear signal: China's commitment to high-standard opening up, to sharing opportunities with the Asia-Pacific, and to multilateralism remains firm," said Chen, who is also a professor at Shenzhen University. A drone photo shows an exterior view of PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material (PT BTR) at Kendal Industrial Park in Central Java province, Indonesia, Aug. 7, 2024. (Xinhua/Xu Qin) BUILDING LOCALLY BTR New Material Group (BTR), a Shenzhen-based battery materials maker, opened an anode material plant in Indonesia's Kendal Industrial Park in August 2024 -- the first overseas anode production base built by a Chinese company in the sector, said He Xueqin, the group's chairman. Before this plant, Indonesia had no lithium-ion battery anode manufacturing industry at all, He said. Then-Indonesian president Joko Widodo attended the opening, saying it brought the country a step closer to building an electric-vehicle ecosystem, the Economic Daily reported at the time. Two years on, a second phase is in full operation, doubling annual capacity to 160,000 tonnes. The Indonesian subsidiary's revenue jumped 161 percent year on year to 1.71 billion yuan in the first half of 2026, supplying battery makers in Japan, the Republic of Korea, Europe and the United States. Before the plant, Indonesia had already built a cathode materials industry from its nickel resources, and BTR added the anode link. "By 2026, separator and electrolyte production has also landed in Indonesia, completing the four main battery materials and laying a solid foundation for the electric-vehicle ecosystem," He said. The deeper shift is what BTR calls "chain-style overseas expansion," with the company having urged its strategic suppliers to move with it, helping them with local research, assessment and site selection. Packaging and crucible suppliers have already set up operations in Indonesia. Shenzhen SED Industry Co., Ltd. (SED), a subsidiary of China Electronics Corporation, is exporting plant-building capability itself. For an optical module project in Thailand, its design team analyzed years of local climate data rather than copying domestic designs, adding safeguards against heat and humidity in everything from equipment selection to insulation and cleanroom airtightness. At an electronics plant in Thailand's 304 Industrial Park, SED applied digital technology across design, construction and operations. Construction clashes fell by more than 95 percent, accidents by over 80 percent, and the plant went from blueprint to completion in just 270 days. The company now has more than 500 staff and over 1,300 overseas supply chain partners across APEC economies including Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia, SED said. Staff members patrol at a plant of Shenzhen SED Industry Co., Ltd. (SED), a subsidiary of China Electronics Corporation, in Thailand in March 2025. (China Electronics Corporation/Handout via Xinhua) RESEARCH AND TALENT New plants need people who can run, maintain and improve them. Shenzhen's ties with the region are therefore extending beyond production lines into laboratories and classrooms. As of March 2026, BGI Group, a Shenzhen-based life science and genomics organization, had jointly trained students with more than 80 universities at home and abroad, including Chulalongkorn University and Mahidol University in Thailand, the University of Indonesia and the University of Malaya. These programs involved 4,490 students in total, 2,503 of them at master's or doctoral level. Such training is tied to research. With Chulalongkorn University, BGI is working on population aging, gut microbiome studies and thalassemia. In Indonesia, BGI signed an agreement in September 2026 with the health ministry's center for biomedical and health genomics to support the Biomedical and Genome Science Initiative, the country's first national genome program, covering joint research, platform development and local training. BGI describes its approach as "using projects to build disciplines, industries and talent." Since 2018, BGI has run 13 national-level training programs for more than 360 mid- and senior-level biotech professionals from Belt and Road partner countries, almost 60 percent of them from APEC members, and several alumni have become senior public health officials at home, the company said. Surgeons perform a robot-assisted surgery in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in September 2026. (Yuanhua Tech/Handout via Xinhua) TECHNOLOGY ON THE GROUND The ultimate test of sci-tech cooperation is whether it can serve local needs and improve everyday life. In a Kuala Lumpur operating room, orthopaedic surgeon Rajiv Rampal guided a Shenzhen-developed robot through a hip replacement. The machine, developed by Shenzhen-based Yuanhua Robotics, Perception and AI Technologies Ltd. (Yuanhua Tech) and manufactured in Hong Kong, completed its first Malaysian operation in July and had performed 21 procedures by early September. Unlike many surgical robots that are tied to specific implant brands, the Shenzhen robot runs on an open platform: all 21 operations used international-brand implants familiar to local doctors. AI algorithms plan for different implant brands, achieving sub-millimeter placement without changing surgeons' routines. "Let the machine adapt to the doctor, not the doctor to the machine," a Yuanhua Tech official said. Shenzhen's rapid technological innovation, coupled with Hong Kong's international quality control standards, gives Malaysia access to cutting-edge medical technology, an official with the Malaysian Chinese-language daily Kwong Wah Yit Poh said. At century-old Mahidol University in Thailand, 41 campus buildings are topped with solar panels. Huawei describes the project as the Asia-Pacific's largest single-site commercial and industrial solar-plus-storage system. This project serves a national goal. Thailand announced at the COP26 climate summit in 2021 that it would achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, and has encouraged rooftop solar via incentives and tighter safety standards. The university chose Huawei's smart photovoltaic solution: 15 megawatts of solar capacity, 600 kilowatt-hours of storage and optimisers, which is expected to save around 2.3 million U.S. dollars a year and cut carbon emissions by 11,000 tonnes. The optimisers allow more panels across the 41 rooftops and lift power output by 10 percent, while the storage provides backup power. The campus is part of a wider footprint. By early 2025, Huawei's digital power business had served over 1,000 Thai enterprises and installed 6 gigawatts of solar inverters, helping generate more than 6 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity and cut carbon dioxide emissions by more than 5 million tonnes, said Yu Junxiang, an official with Huawei's arm in Thailand. Taken together, Chen said, these cases show how Shenzhen, an urban test case for Chinese modernization, can serve a region: openness breeds cooperation and innovation drives shared growth, offering Asia-Pacific economies a viable path to build consensus, narrow development gaps and achieve shared prosperity. item.title: "China, Thailand as close as one family" a unique advantage of bilateral ties, says Chinese premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
"China, Thailand as close as one family" a unique advantage of bilateral ties, says Chinese premier Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 14, 2026. (Xinhua) BANGKOK, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that "China and Thailand are as close as one family" is a unique advantage of bilateral relations, as reflected in the practical achievements across various fields. Li made the remarks during his meeting with Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn in Bangkok. Conveying cordial greetings from Chinese President Xi Jinping to the king, Li said that during the king's state visit to China last year, Xi held talks with him, and the two sides reached important consensus on advancing the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future. China appreciates that the Thai royal family has long attached great importance to and remained committed to promoting China-Thailand friendship, Li said. He noted that the continued growth of China-Thailand economic and trade cooperation despite headwinds is particularly commendable amid the current turbulent international situation. Li said that China stands ready to work with Thailand, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, to maintain close exchanges, expand cooperation in investment, technological innovation, new energy vehicles and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, and promote economic and social development in both countries for the greater well-being of their peoples. The Thai king asked Li to convey his sincere greetings and best wishes to President Xi. Recalling his state visit to China last year, the king said that the successful meeting with Xi was fruitful and remained fresh in his memory. Li's official visit to Thailand would help further consolidate the traditional friendship between Thailand and China and deepen practical cooperation between the two countries, the king said. item.title: China expects greater consensus, more tangible outcomes with APEC parties: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China expects greater consensus, more tangible outcomes with APEC parties: spokesperson BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- China looks forward to building further consensus among parties of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), achieving more tangible outcomes, and injecting robust impetus into prosperity and growth in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Friday. Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular press briefing when answering a query related to the upcoming 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Noting that after 12 years, China is once again hosting APEC, Mao said the APEC "China Year" has yielded fruitful outcomes. China has successfully held over 300 meetings and events by focusing on the theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together" and the three priority areas of "Openness, Innovation, and Cooperation." More than 10,000 representatives have participated in the events and reached a number of common understandings on cooperation, laying a solid foundation for the upcoming meeting, said the spokesperson. With this APEC meeting set to open next week, Mao said China looks forward to agreeing on the APEC Shenzhen Leaders' Declaration among all member economies as well as more practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, and artificial intelligence. item.title: China's top diplomat meets U.S. representatives attending political dialogue
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China's top diplomat meets U.S. representatives attending political dialogue Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, meets with U.S. representatives attending the U.S.-China Political Dialogue 2026 in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu) BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- China's top diplomat Wang Yi on Friday met with U.S. representatives attending the U.S.-China Political Dialogue 2026 in Beijing. Wang, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, said that China and the United States should clarify the goals of their joint efforts, expand the areas of mutually beneficial cooperation, consolidate the foundation of bilateral relations, and be committed to maintaining world peace and stability. The two sides should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win-win cooperation, and implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state on building a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity, Wang noted. The representative of the U.S. side said that people-to-people and cultural exchanges, especially those between young people and students, are conducive to enhancing friendship and mutual trust between the two peoples, adding that they are grateful for the invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study in the coming five years, and are willing to make efforts to promote the healthy and stable development of U.S.-China relations. item.title: China willing to further boost political mutual trust with Thailand, says Chinese premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China willing to further boost political mutual trust with Thailand, says Chinese premier Chinese Premier Li Qiang holds talks with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) BANGKOK, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Friday that China is willing to work with Thailand to further consolidate the foundation of political mutual trust, support each other's core interests and major concerns, tap cooperation potential in various fields and deliver more tangible results to better benefit the peoples of both countries. Li made the remarks when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. He said Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Anutin during the Thai PM's official visit to China in July, and the two leaders jointly charted the course for the development of China-Thailand relations. Li said that, with his visit to Thailand, the prime ministers of the two countries have exchanged visits within four months, fully demonstrating the high level of bilateral relations. Noting that both China and Thailand are at an important stage of national development, Li said China firmly supports the Thai government in smoothly carrying out its work. China is willing to work with Thailand to make good use of mechanisms such as the "2+2" strategic dialogue between foreign and defense ministers and the joint committee on economic and trade cooperation, Li said. China stands ready to work with Thailand to strengthen the alignment of development strategies, advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and key projects such as the China-Thailand railway, and accelerate consultations on a new five-year plan for economic and trade cooperation, Li said. He added that China is ready to promote the early realization of mutual protection of geographical indication products, and expand cooperation in such fields as finance, new energy, semiconductors, and artificial intelligence, so as to achieve mutual benefit and win-win outcomes at a higher level. China is ready to import more quality products from Thailand and encourages Chinese companies to invest and do business in the Southeast Asian country, he said, adding that China hopes the Thai side will provide a fair, stable and predictable business environment for Chinese companies. The two sides, Li said, should also strengthen exchanges and cooperation in areas including disaster prevention and mitigation, water resources management, education, tourism and media, and step up efforts to combat illegal and criminal activities, to enhance the people's sense of gain from China-Thailand cooperation. At present, the international situation remains fraught with instability and uncertainty, Li said, noting that China is willing to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Thailand under multilateral frameworks including China-ASEAN, the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation, the United Nations, the World Trade Organization and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, so as to contribute to global peace and development. For his part, Anutin said Thailand attaches great importance to its relations with China and is committed to advancing all-round cooperation between the two countries and continuously elevating the Thailand-China comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership to new heights, bringing greater benefits to the two peoples. Thailand is willing to strengthen high-level exchanges with China, make good use of mechanisms such as the "2+2" strategic dialogue between foreign and defense ministers of the two countries, expand bilateral trade, and deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in fields including agriculture, finance, connectivity, electric vehicles, artificial intelligence, e-commerce, and science and technology, said the Thai prime minister. Thailand is ready to continue providing a favorable business environment for Chinese enterprises investing in Thailand, strengthen law enforcement and security cooperation with China to combat online gambling, telecom and online fraud among other crimes, ensure the safety of Chinese tourists, and deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges to consolidate the foundation of public friendship, Anutin said. Thailand supports China's successful hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and stands ready to work with China to ensure the success of the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Leaders' Meeting, making new contributions to regional stability, development and prosperity, said the Thai prime minister. Following the talks, the two leaders witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering the fields including the automotive industry, vocational education, agriculture, customs and security. Chinese Premier Li Qiang holds talks with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added.
